# VirtualContainer Class

> [!CAUTION]
> This class is still in pre-release.  Its signature may change or it may be removed in future releases.

## Extends
- [*Container*](Container.md)

A container that only exists in memory. It is not tied to a block, an entity or the world, is never saved, and is destroyed once the script no longer references it and no player is viewing it. It supports the full Container API and can be shown to any number of players at once with open. When the world shuts down or scripts reload, open screens close without raising close events; save the contents from system.beforeEvents.shutdown if they need to outlive the session.

## Properties

### **title**
`read-only title: string;`

The heading shown on the container screen. It is localized when it names a localization key.

Type: *string*

### **close**
`
close(player?: Player): number
`

Requests closure of the container screen of a player, or of every player viewing this container when no player is given. From then on, those players can no longer change the container through their screens. Each screen raises a VirtualContainerCloseAfterEvent with the ServerClosed reason after the client has closed its UI and pending inventory requests have finished. Closure may complete on a later tick.

#### **Parameters**
- **player**?: [*Player*](Player.md) = `null`
  
  The player whose screen to close. When omitted, every viewer's screen is closed.

**Returns** *number* - The number of screens asked to close. A screen that is already closing is not counted again.
  
Notes:
- This function can't be called in restricted-execution mode.
- This function can throw errors.
  - Throws [*InvalidEntityError*](InvalidEntityError.md)

### **getViewers**
`
getViewers(): Player[]
`

Gets the players currently viewing this container.

**Returns** [*Player*](Player.md)[] - The players that have a screen open onto this container.

### **open**
`
open(player: Player): void
`

Shows a chest style screen onto this container to a player. Only that player sees the screen; any number of players can view the same container at once, each with a screen of their own. Changing dimension closes the screen with the ServerClosed reason, dying closes it with the PlayerDied reason, and switching to spectator mode closes it with the PlayerSpectating reason.

#### **Parameters**
- **player**: [*Player*](Player.md)
  
  The player to show the container to.
  
Notes:
- This function can't be called in restricted-execution mode.
- This function can throw errors.
  - Throws [*@minecraft/common.EngineError*](../../../scriptapi/minecraft/common/EngineError.md), [*InvalidEntityError*](InvalidEntityError.md), [*VirtualContainerOpenError*](VirtualContainerOpenError.md)
